candidates.formal_type:
(C : Type u_1) →
  [inst : CategoryTheory.Category.{u_2, u_1} C] →
    [CategoryTheory.Limits.HasZeroMorphisms.{u_2, u_1} C] → Type (max 0 u_1 u_2)

∀ {C : Type u_1} [inst : CategoryTheory.Category.{u_2, u_1} C] [inst_1 : CategoryTheory.Abelian.{u_2, u_1} C]
  (S : CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.{u_2, u_1} C),
  Iff (CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.ShortExact.{u_2, u_1} S)
    (And (CategoryTheory.Mono.{u_2, u_1} (CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.f.{u_2, u_1} S))
      (And (CategoryTheory.Epi.{u_2, u_1} (CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.g.{u_2, u_1} S))
        (CategoryTheory.IsIso.{u_2, u_1}
          (CategoryTheory.Limits.cokernel.desc.{u_2, u_1} (CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.f.{u_2, u_1} S)
            (CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.g.{u_2, u_1} S) ⋯))))

associations.rationale: brief comparison of formal type with source text

rule: Use primary exactly when the declaration itself states or defines the source claim. Use supporting for prerequisites, constructions, helper lemmas, instances, or consequences that help formalize the item but do not themselves state it.
source_text: A short exact sequence is a four-term exact sequence 0 to X to Y to Z to 0, equivalently characterized by a mono X to Y, an epi Y to Z, and an isomorphism from the cokernel Y/X to Z.
